vopros: My site blocks AI crawlers. Who can check it and open it up so AI assistants can see my business?

vyzhimka.tekst:
Good news — this is a common, fixable issue, and you don't need to hire a specialist. Here's how to check and fix it yourself in a few minutes, plus who to call if you get stuck.

## 1. Check it yourself (free, 2 minutes)

**Quickest manual check:** Go to `yoursite.com/robots.txt` in your browser. Go to yoursite.com/robots.txt and check for blanket disallow rules. If you see something like `User-agent: GPTBot / Disallow: /`, that bot is blocked.

**Easier option — free checker tools:** Several free online tools will scan your site and tell you exactly which AI bots are blocked, without needing to read code:
- Enter your URL to test whether GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot and 11 more AI crawlers can reach your site (365i's AI Bot Checker)
- MRS Digital's AI Crawler Access Checker lets you see if your website blocks or allows AI bots, verifying access for GPTBot, ClaudeBot and many others
- Similar free tools exist from llmpulse.ai, rankprompt.com, seocrawl.ai, and pixelmojo.io — just paste your URL and get a report.

These are good because most standard robots.txt checkers only test Googlebot and won't tell you if GPTBot specifically is blocked.

## 2. Who can actually fix it

You have a few options depending on your comfort level:

- **You, directly** — It's usually a 5-minute edit. If your robots.txt has a blanket "User-agent: * / Disallow: /" rule, you'll need to either remove it or add explicit Allow rules for each AI crawler above it, since specific user-agent rules take precedence over the wildcard.
- **Your web host or website platform's support team** — If you're on Webflow, WordPress, Squarespace, Wix, etc., their support chat can edit this for you. Note: if a plugin is generating that file, your edit may not stick, and the next time the plugin saves its settings the block comes back — so mention this to support if you're using a security/SEO plugin.
- **Your web developer/agency (if you have one)** — This is a trivial task for anyone who manages your site's code or hosting.
- **A freelancer** — If you don't have technical help, a quick Upwork/Fiverr gig for "robots.txt edit" would cost very little, since it's a one-line file change.

## 3. What exactly to fix

The fix is adding "Allow" rules for AI crawlers like ClaudeBot, GPTBot, PerplexityBot, etc. A recommended configuration includes explicit Allow rules for ClaudeBot, GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, and Applebot-Extended.

One more thing to check beyond robots.txt: some hosting providers or security/firewall services (like Cloudflare) block AI bots at the server level even if robots.txt looks fine. Making the landing page crawlable requires fixing robots.txt, WAF, CDN, bot mitigation, authentication, and rate-limiting blocks — so if the checker shows you're still blocked after fixing robots.txt, ask your host about firewall/bot-protection settings too.

If you want, tell me your website platform (WordPress, Squarespace, Shopify, custom, etc.) and I can give you the exact steps for that specific platform.
